      <h1>Instruction Hierarchy Design Canvas</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A target instruction hierarchy with at least three specificity levels, and the migration list for flattening or splitting what exists today.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-13-instruction-hierarchy-canvas</b><br>
      Pack Z - Second wave: the practitioner kit<br>
      fill order <b>6</b> &middot; type <b>canvas</b><br>
      audience <b>architect</b>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>The PROSE Constraints</b>, <i>E &mdash; Explicit Hierarchy</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.qmd</code> L295-370 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.html#sec-prose-explicit-hierarchy">#sec-prose-explicit-hierarchy</a>
    &middot; prerequisite: <code>WS-03-context-moat-asset-inventory</code> (its classified rule list is surface B's row set)
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Sketch the target instruction hierarchy for one real repository. Start with the diagnostic box below, and fill it out loud
    before anything else. Then, on sheets 2 and 3, put each node in the tree: what belongs at the root (true everywhere), at each
    domain, and at each module. For every rule your repository holds globally today, decide whether to keep it, scope it down or
    delete it. At each level apply one test: can module-specific rules be added without editing any file above that module?
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>What the book prints &mdash; read before drawing
      <span class="ws-block-note">reference only; nothing to write here</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:50%"><col style="width:50%">
      </colgroup>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="prior"><b>The worked four-level tree</b> (root, <code>frontend/</code>, <code>frontend/components/</code>, <code>backend/</code>, <code>backend/auth/</code>)<br>
            <code>project/AGENTS.md</code> &mdash; Global: naming, commits, documentation<br>
            <code>&nbsp;&nbsp;frontend/AGENTS.md</code> &mdash; Frontend: React patterns, accessibility<br>
            <code>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;frontend/components/AGENTS.md</code> &mdash; Components: prop conventions, testing<br>
            <code>&nbsp;&nbsp;backend/AGENTS.md</code> &mdash; Backend: API design, error handling<br>
            <code>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;backend/auth/AGENTS.md</code> &mdash; Auth: security patterns, token handling<span class="prior-src">ch13 L304-314</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><b>The resolution walk.</b> An agent editing <code>backend/auth/token.py</code> resolves <code>auth/AGENTS.md</code> + <code>backend/AGENTS.md</code> + root <code>AGENTS.md</code>. An agent editing <code>frontend/components/Button.tsx</code> resolves <code>components/AGENTS.md</code> + <code>frontend/AGENTS.md</code> + root <code>AGENTS.md</code>. Neither loads the other's domain-specific rules.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L316</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="prior"><b>Two scope forms.</b> Directory placement: a file at the root applies everywhere; <code>frontend/AGENTS.md</code> applies only to frontend code. Pattern: <code>applyTo: "**/*.py"</code>, then <code>"src/api/**/*.py"</code>, then <code>"src/api/auth/**/*.py"</code> &mdash; more specific patterns override or extend less specific ones.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L301-337</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><b>Three mechanisms.</b> Directory-scoped <code>AGENTS.md</code>; <code>applyTo</code> pattern; authored then compiled. The authored instructions are the source of truth; the compiled output is the portable delivery format.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L301, L318, L339</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="prior"><b>The filled three-level sample.</b> Root: TypeScript strict mode, Conventional Commits, JSDoc on public functions, links to error and testing docs. Backend: <code>asyncHandler</code> wrapper, Zod validation of request bodies, database access only through repository classes. Auth module (<code>applyTo: "src/auth/**"</code>): RS256 token signing, single-use refresh tokens, never log token values, a STOP gate before changing signing or rotation.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L410-474</span></td>
          <td class="prior"><b>The fix for a flat file.</b> Split by scope. Python rules in a Python-scoped file, React rules in a frontend-scoped file, authentication rules in an auth-scoped file. Each agent loads only what applies to its current task. <b>Before/after:</b> bare inlined sections become labelled pointers, e.g. "Authentication patterns and token lifecycle".<span class="prior-src">ch13 L91-102, L368</span></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
